paragraphs.title: The Lord Appears and Abraham Welcomes His Guests

easy.question: Where was Abraham sitting at the beginning of the passage?
answers: At the tent door
Under the tree
Inside the city
easy.explanation: The first verse says that Abraham sat at the tent door.

easy.question: How many men did Abraham see?
answers: Three
Two
Four
easy.explanation: The verse says, “three men stood by him.”

easy.question: What did Abraham do when he saw the men?
answers: He entered the tent
He went to sleep
He ran to meet them and bowed
easy.explanation: Abraham ran to meet the men and bowed himself to the ground.

medium.question: What did Abraham do immediately after seeing the three men?
answers: He ran to meet them and bowed
He brought them bread
He asked them to leave
medium.explanation: Abraham first ran to meet the men and bowed before offering hospitality.

medium.question: Why did Abraham offer the men water, washed feet, and rest?
answers: To test them
To refresh them after their journey
To make them stay a long time
medium.explanation: These things would comfort and refresh the travelers.

medium.question: In the phrase “comfort ye your hearts,” what does “comfort” mean?
answers: Leave immediately
Hide yourselves
Be refreshed and strengthened
medium.explanation: The bread was meant to refresh them and give them strength for the journey.

challenge.question: What can we infer from Abraham’s running to meet the men even though it was “the heat of the day”?
answers: He was eager and ready to show hospitality
He was afraid of them
He wanted to flee the tent
challenge.explanation: Despite the intense heat, Abraham hurried to welcome his guests.

challenge.question: What do Abraham’s words, “pass not away, I pray thee, from thy servant,” express?
answers: Anger at the men
Humility and a request that they stay
A desire to travel with them
challenge.explanation: By calling himself their servant and asking them not to pass on, Abraham shows humility and hospitality.

challenge.question: Which detail shows that Abraham wanted the guests to be comfortable before continuing their journey?
answers: He sat at the tent door
He lifted up his eyes
He offered water, washed feet, rest, and bread
challenge.explanation: Abraham’s offers provided refreshment, rest, and food before they continued.

questions.question: What can we infer from Abraham’s running to meet the men even though it was “the heat of the day”?
answers: He was eager and ready to show hospitality
He was afraid of them
He wanted to flee the tent
questions.explanation: Despite the intense heat, Abraham hurried to welcome his guests.

questions.question: What do Abraham’s words, “pass not away, I pray thee, from thy servant,” express?
answers: Anger at the men
Humility and a request that they stay
A desire to travel with them
questions.explanation: By calling himself their servant and asking them not to pass on, Abraham shows humility and hospitality.

questions.question: Which detail shows that Abraham wanted the guests to be comfortable before continuing their journey?
answers: He sat at the tent door
He lifted up his eyes
He offered water, washed feet, rest, and bread
questions.explanation: Abraham’s offers provided refreshment, rest, and food before they continued.

paragraphs.title: Preparing a Meal for the Guests

easy.question: Whom did Abraham tell to prepare cakes?
answers: Sarah
The young man
The guests
easy.explanation: Abraham told Sarah, “Make ready quickly... knead it, and make cakes.”

easy.question: What did Abraham prepare from the herd?
answers: A lamb
A tender calf
A fish
easy.explanation: Abraham took a tender and good calf and had it prepared.

easy.question: Where did Abraham stand while the guests ate?
answers: Inside the tent
By the well
Under the tree
easy.explanation: The verse says that Abraham stood by them under the tree.

medium.question: What does Abraham and Sarah’s haste in preparing the food show?
answers: They wanted to honor the guests promptly
They did not want the guests to eat
They were waiting for the guests to leave
medium.explanation: The repeated emphasis on haste shows their eagerness to welcome the guests.

medium.question: In the phrase “knead it,” what was Sarah told to do?
answers: Eat it
Work the dough
Take the calf
medium.explanation: Sarah was told to knead the meal into dough for the cakes.

medium.question: What was the order of events?
answers: The guests ate, and then Sarah made cakes
The young man prepared the calf, and then Abraham took it
Sarah made cakes, Abraham prepared a calf, and the food was served
medium.explanation: Sarah prepared the cakes, Abraham provided the calf, and then the meal was served.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “a calf tender and good” show about Abraham’s choice?
answers: He chose excellent meat for the guests
He chose an old animal
He did not know what to choose
challenge.explanation: The words “tender and good” emphasize the quality of the calf.

challenge.question: According to the sequence of the verse, who stood under the tree while the guests ate?
answers: The young man
Abraham
Sarah
challenge.explanation: Abraham served the food and then stood by the guests under the tree.

challenge.question: What idea is shown by Abraham handling the calf himself but giving it to the young man to prepare?
answers: He personally participated in the hospitality while delegating a task
He had no involvement in the meal
The young man was the household head
challenge.explanation: Abraham acted personally but also assigned the preparation to the young man.

questions.question: What does the phrase “a calf tender and good” show about Abraham’s choice?
answers: He chose excellent meat for the guests
He chose an old animal
He did not know what to choose
questions.explanation: The words “tender and good” emphasize the quality of the calf.

questions.question: According to the sequence of the verse, who stood under the tree while the guests ate?
answers: The young man
Abraham
Sarah
questions.explanation: Abraham served the food and then stood by the guests under the tree.

questions.question: What idea is shown by Abraham handling the calf himself but giving it to the young man to prepare?
answers: He personally participated in the hospitality while delegating a task
He had no involvement in the meal
The young man was the household head
questions.explanation: Abraham acted personally but also assigned the preparation to the young man.

paragraphs.title: The Promise of Isaac and Sarah’s Laughter

easy.question: Where was Sarah when Abraham spoke with the guests?
answers: In the tent
In the field
In the city house
easy.explanation: Abraham answered, “Behold, in the tent,” indicating where Sarah was.

easy.question: What news was given Abraham about Sarah?
answers: She would leave on a journey
She would have a son
She would build a new tent
easy.explanation: The visitor said, “Sarah thy wife shall have a son.”

easy.question: Who laughed when she heard that she would have a son?
answers: One of the servants
Lot’s wife
Sarah
easy.explanation: The verse plainly says, “Sarah laughed within herself.”

medium.question: Why did Sarah find it difficult to believe that she would have a son?
answers: She and Abraham were old, and she was past childbearing age
She did not want a son
She did not know who was speaking
medium.explanation: Sarah considered their old age and the fact that she was past the usual time of childbearing.

medium.question: What is the correct order of events?
answers: Sarah denied it, the guests asked about her, and then a son was promised
The guests asked about Sarah, a son was promised, and Sarah laughed
Sarah laughed, the son was born, and then the guests asked about her
medium.explanation: The guests asked about Sarah, promised a son, and Sarah then laughed inwardly.

medium.question: In the verse, “At the time appointed,” what does “appointed” mean?
answers: A distant place
A special reason
A set or predetermined time
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the time when the promise would be fulfilled.

challenge.question: What is emphasized by the promises, “I will certainly return unto thee” and “At the time appointed I will return unto thee”?
answers: The promise concerns a specific time when Sarah will have a son
The guests wanted Abraham to leave immediately
Sarah would wait many years without a promise
challenge.explanation: The repeated reference to a set time emphasizes that the son would be born according to God’s promise.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the difference between Sarah’s laughter and her later answer?
answers: She laughed aloud publicly and was unafraid
She laughed inwardly and then denied it because she was afraid
She did not laugh at all, and the guests were mistaken
challenge.explanation: Sarah laughed within herself and later denied it because she was afraid.

challenge.question: What does the question “Is any thing too hard for the Lord?” mean here?
answers: Can Sarah hide her thoughts?
Will Abraham find the tent?
Is anything too difficult or impossible for the Lord?
challenge.explanation: The question teaches that nothing is impossible for the Lord, including Sarah’s having a son in old age.

questions.question: What is emphasized by the promises, “I will certainly return unto thee” and “At the time appointed I will return unto thee”?
answers: The promise concerns a specific time when Sarah will have a son
The guests wanted Abraham to leave immediately
Sarah would wait many years without a promise
questions.explanation: The repeated reference to a set time emphasizes that the son would be born according to God’s promise.

questions.question: What can we infer from the difference between Sarah’s laughter and her later answer?
answers: She laughed aloud publicly and was unafraid
She laughed inwardly and then denied it because she was afraid
She did not laugh at all, and the guests were mistaken
questions.explanation: Sarah laughed within herself and later denied it because she was afraid.

questions.question: What does the question “Is any thing too hard for the Lord?” mean here?
answers: Can Sarah hide her thoughts?
Will Abraham find the tent?
Is anything too difficult or impossible for the Lord?
questions.explanation: The question teaches that nothing is impossible for the Lord, including Sarah’s having a son in old age.

paragraphs.title: Abraham’s Calling to Justice and Righteousness

easy.question: Who went with the men to send them on their way?
answers: Abraham
Lot
Isaac
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Abraham went with them to bring them on the way.”

easy.question: Which city did the men look toward?
answers: Hebron
Sodom
Egypt
easy.explanation: The men looked toward Sodom.

easy.question: What was said about Abraham and the nations?
answers: Abraham would leave his land
Abraham would rule all nations
Abraham would become a great nation, and all nations would be blessed in him
easy.explanation: The passage says Abraham would become a great and mighty nation, and all nations would be blessed in him.

medium.question: Why did the Lord not want to hide from Abraham what He was about to do?
answers: Abraham would become a great nation and teach his household the Lord’s way
Abraham had asked to see Sodom
Abraham had gone with the men
medium.explanation: The Lord says Abraham would command his household to do justice and judgment.

medium.question: In “they shall keep the way of the Lord,” what does “keep” mean?
answers: Hide the Lord’s way
Leave the Lord’s way
Follow and observe the Lord’s way
medium.explanation: Here, “keep” means to follow faithfully and observe the Lord’s way.

medium.question: What is the sequence described in these verses?
answers: Abraham commanded his children, and then the men rose
The men rose and looked toward Sodom, and Abraham went with them
The nations were blessed, and then Abraham arrived in Sodom
medium.explanation: The men rose and looked toward Sodom while Abraham went with them.

challenge.question: What is the connection between the Lord’s knowing Abraham and Abraham’s role?
answers: Abraham was chosen to teach his household justice and righteousness
Abraham was chosen because he lived near Sodom
Abraham was chosen because he knew the future
challenge.explanation: The Lord knew Abraham would command his household to keep His way and do justice.

challenge.question: What does “that” express in “that the Lord may bring upon Abraham”?
answers: The time of the event
The purpose or intended result
The place of the event
challenge.explanation: The phrase describes the purpose of Abraham’s instruction and faithfulness.

challenge.question: What moral condition is emphasized as part of Abraham’s continuing calling?
answers: That he would conquer many lands
That he would hide his actions from his household
That his household would keep the Lord’s way and do justice
challenge.explanation: The promise is connected with Abraham’s household following the Lord’s way and doing justice.

questions.question: What is the connection between the Lord’s knowing Abraham and Abraham’s role?
answers: Abraham was chosen to teach his household justice and righteousness
Abraham was chosen because he lived near Sodom
Abraham was chosen because he knew the future
questions.explanation: The Lord knew Abraham would command his household to keep His way and do justice.

questions.question: What does “that” express in “that the Lord may bring upon Abraham”?
answers: The time of the event
The purpose or intended result
The place of the event
questions.explanation: The phrase describes the purpose of Abraham’s instruction and faithfulness.

questions.question: What moral condition is emphasized as part of Abraham’s continuing calling?
answers: That he would conquer many lands
That he would hide his actions from his household
That his household would keep the Lord’s way and do justice
questions.explanation: The promise is connected with Abraham’s household following the Lord’s way and doing justice.

paragraphs.title: The Cry of Sodom and Divine Investigation

easy.question: Which cities are mentioned in these verses?
answers: Sodom and Gomorrah
Bethel and Hebron
Egypt and Canaan
easy.explanation: The verse explicitly mentions Sodom and Gomorrah.

easy.question: What does the Lord say He will do concerning Sodom’s deeds?
answers: Send men to the cities
Go down and see whether their deeds are as reported
Bless the people of the city
easy.explanation: The Lord says, “I will go down now, and see.”

easy.question: What did Abraham do after the men turned and went toward Sodom?
answers: He followed them
He returned home
He still stood before the Lord
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Abraham stood yet before the Lord.”

medium.question: Why does the Lord say, “I will go down now, and see”?
answers: To determine whether the deeds matched the cry that had come to Him
To invite the people of Sodom to a meal
To find a new place to live
medium.explanation: The Lord describes examining whether the people had truly acted according to the cry.

medium.question: What happened after the men turned away?
answers: Abraham went to Sodom while the men stayed
The men went toward Sodom, and Abraham remained before the Lord
Everyone returned to where they had come from
medium.explanation: The men went toward Sodom, while Abraham remained before the Lord.

medium.question: In “their sin is very grievous,” what does “grievous” mean?
answers: Gone
Forgotten
Very serious and severe
medium.explanation: The word describes sin that is extremely serious.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the words, “and if not, I will know”?
answers: The Lord intends to examine whether reality matches the cry He heard
The Lord has already decided to save the city
Abraham does not know where Sodom is
challenge.explanation: The words describe an investigation rather than reliance on a report alone.

challenge.question: What is the difference between “the cry of Sodom and Gomorrah” and “their sin”?
answers: The cry is the name of a city, while sin is the name of a person
The cry is the complaint that reached the Lord, while the sin describes the people’s deeds
They have no connection
challenge.explanation: The passage refers both to the cry that reached the Lord and to the serious sins that caused it.

challenge.question: What does “yet” emphasize in “Abraham stood yet before the Lord”?
answers: Abraham had only just arrived
Abraham had been standing before the men arrived
Abraham continued standing before the Lord after the men left
challenge.explanation: “Yet” emphasizes that Abraham’s standing before the Lord continued after the men departed.

questions.question: What can we infer from the words, “and if not, I will know”?
answers: The Lord intends to examine whether reality matches the cry He heard
The Lord has already decided to save the city
Abraham does not know where Sodom is
questions.explanation: The words describe an investigation rather than reliance on a report alone.

questions.question: What is the difference between “the cry of Sodom and Gomorrah” and “their sin”?
answers: The cry is the name of a city, while sin is the name of a person
The cry is the complaint that reached the Lord, while the sin describes the people’s deeds
They have no connection
questions.explanation: The passage refers both to the cry that reached the Lord and to the serious sins that caused it.

questions.question: What does “yet” emphasize in “Abraham stood yet before the Lord”?
answers: Abraham had only just arrived
Abraham had been standing before the men arrived
Abraham continued standing before the Lord after the men left
questions.explanation: “Yet” emphasizes that Abraham’s standing before the Lord continued after the men departed.

easy.question: Who drew near to speak with the Lord?
answers: Abraham
Lot
Moses
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Abraham drew near, and said.”

easy.question: How many righteous people did Abraham mention at first?
answers: Ten
Fifty
One hundred
easy.explanation: Abraham asked about fifty righteous people in the city.

easy.question: What would the Lord do if fifty righteous people were found in Sodom?
answers: Punish only the righteous
Remove everyone from the city
Spare the whole place for their sake
easy.explanation: The Lord said He would spare the whole place for their sake.

medium.question: Why did Abraham object to destroying Sodom with the righteous?
answers: He believed it was unjust for the righteous to be punished with the wicked
He wanted to move there
He thought there were no wicked people in the city
medium.explanation: Abraham argued that the righteous should not be destroyed together with the wicked.

medium.question: In “wilt thou also destroy and not spare the place,” what does “spare” mean?
answers: Destroy
Show mercy and save
Leave
medium.explanation: Here, “spare” means to show mercy and preserve the place.

medium.question: What is the correct sequence?
answers: The Lord announced fifty righteous people, and then Abraham drew near
Abraham asked for the city to be spared for fifty righteous people, and the Lord agreed
Abraham asked the Lord to punish the righteous, and the Lord refused
medium.explanation: Abraham made the request, and the Lord agreed to spare the place if fifty righteous people were found.

challenge.question: What moral principle appears in Abraham’s claim, “Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right?”
answers: Justice must distinguish between the righteous and the wicked
Everyone in the city must receive the same punishment
There is no need for judgment
challenge.explanation: Abraham insists that the righteous should not be punished with the wicked.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the Lord’s answer in verse 26?
answers: The righteous must leave Sodom
A small group of righteous people could bring salvation to the whole city
The Lord would not listen to Abraham
challenge.explanation: The Lord says He would spare the whole place for the sake of fifty righteous people.

challenge.question: What is significant about Abraham saying “the righteous with the wicked” rather than merely asking to save the righteous?
answers: He asks that the two groups be distinguished morally
He claims that everyone in Sodom is righteous
He asks that the righteous be punished first
challenge.explanation: Abraham argues that the righteous should not be included in the same punishment as the wicked.

questions.question: What moral principle appears in Abraham’s claim, “Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right?”
answers: Justice must distinguish between the righteous and the wicked
Everyone in the city must receive the same punishment
There is no need for judgment
questions.explanation: Abraham insists that the righteous should not be punished with the wicked.

questions.question: What can we infer from the Lord’s answer in verse 26?
answers: The righteous must leave Sodom
A small group of righteous people could bring salvation to the whole city
The Lord would not listen to Abraham
questions.explanation: The Lord says He would spare the whole place for the sake of fifty righteous people.

questions.question: What is significant about Abraham saying “the righteous with the wicked” rather than merely asking to save the righteous?
answers: He asks that the two groups be distinguished morally
He claims that everyone in Sodom is righteous
He asks that the righteous be punished first
questions.explanation: Abraham argues that the righteous should not be included in the same punishment as the wicked.

paragraphs.title: Lowering the Number and Continuing Abraham’s Appeal

easy.question: Who speaks with the Lord in these verses?
answers: Abraham
Moses
Isaac
easy.explanation: The passage begins, “Abraham answered and said.”

easy.question: What does Abraham compare himself to?
answers: Water and wind
Dust and ashes
Gold and silver
easy.explanation: Abraham says, “I am but dust and ashes,” expressing humility.

easy.question: How many righteous people does Abraham mention in verse 30?
answers: Fifty
Forty
Thirty
easy.explanation: Abraham asks whether thirty righteous people might be found there.

medium.question: What does Abraham express by saying, “I am but dust and ashes”?
answers: Humility and reverence before the Lord
Anger at the people of the city
Joy at his success
medium.explanation: Abraham emphasizes his smallness and humility before continuing his request.

medium.question: If five are missing from fifty righteous people, how many remain?
answers: Forty
Forty-five
Thirty-five
medium.explanation: Fifty minus five is forty-five.

medium.question: In “I have taken upon me to speak unto the Lord,” what does the phrase mean?
answers: I forgot
I became angry
I have dared or permitted myself to speak
medium.explanation: Abraham respectfully says that he has dared to speak before the Lord.

challenge.question: What can we infer from moving from fifty righteous people to forty-five, forty, and thirty?
answers: Abraham seeks mercy even if fewer righteous people are found
Abraham changes the city he is discussing
Abraham immediately gives up on the people
challenge.explanation: The gradual decrease shows Abraham continuing to seek the city’s preservation.

challenge.question: What does the Lord’s answer, “I will not do it for forty’s sake,” show about justice and mercy?
answers: The Lord does not listen to requests
The Lord is willing to spare the city for the sake of its righteous people
The city will be saved only if every resident is righteous
challenge.explanation: The Lord agrees not to destroy the city if forty righteous people are found.

challenge.question: What can we understand from “Oh let not the Lord be angry, and I will speak” before Abraham mentions thirty?
answers: Abraham plans to stop speaking
Abraham fears the city has already been destroyed
Abraham speaks carefully and respectfully before making another request
challenge.explanation: He asks the Lord not to be angry as he cautiously continues his appeal.

questions.question: What can we infer from moving from fifty righteous people to forty-five, forty, and thirty?
answers: Abraham seeks mercy even if fewer righteous people are found
Abraham changes the city he is discussing
Abraham immediately gives up on the people
questions.explanation: The gradual decrease shows Abraham continuing to seek the city’s preservation.

questions.question: What does the Lord’s answer, “I will not do it for forty’s sake,” show about justice and mercy?
answers: The Lord does not listen to requests
The Lord is willing to spare the city for the sake of its righteous people
The city will be saved only if every resident is righteous
questions.explanation: The Lord agrees not to destroy the city if forty righteous people are found.

questions.question: What can we understand from “Oh let not the Lord be angry, and I will speak” before Abraham mentions thirty?
answers: Abraham plans to stop speaking
Abraham fears the city has already been destroyed
Abraham speaks carefully and respectfully before making another request
questions.explanation: He asks the Lord not to be angry as he cautiously continues his appeal.

paragraphs.title: Abraham’s Request for the Sake of Twenty

easy.question: How many people did the speaker hope would be found in the city?
answers: Twenty
Thirty
Ten
easy.explanation: The speaker says, “Peradventure there shall be twenty found there.”

easy.question: What was promised if twenty were found there?
answers: The city would be rebuilt
It would not be destroyed
Everyone would leave
easy.explanation: The answer was, “I will not destroy it for twenty’s sake.”

easy.question: For whose sake would the city not be destroyed?
answers: The king’s
Abraham’s
The twenty
easy.explanation: The verse says it would not be destroyed for the sake of the twenty.

medium.question: What is the connection between finding twenty people and not destroying the city?
answers: Finding twenty is the reason the city would be spared
Finding twenty would cause destruction
There is no connection
medium.explanation: The speaker asks that the city be spared if twenty are found, and the request is granted.

medium.question: In “I have taken upon me to speak unto my Lord,” what does the phrase mean?
answers: I forgot to speak
I have dared or permitted myself to speak
I have stopped speaking
medium.explanation: The speaker respectfully asks permission to continue speaking.

medium.question: What is the order of events in the verse?
answers: Twenty were found, and then the speaker asked
The city was destroyed, and then a promise was given
The speaker made the request, and then received the answer that the city would not be destroyed
medium.explanation: The request comes first, followed by the promise to spare the city.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the word “Peradventure”?
answers: The speaker is not certain that twenty will be found
The speaker is certain that twenty will be found
The speaker knows that no one will be found
challenge.explanation: “Peradventure” expresses possibility or uncertainty.

challenge.question: What does “for twenty’s sake” mean in this context?
answers: After twenty years have passed
For the sake of or because of twenty people
Because the city is twenty miles away
challenge.explanation: The city would be spared because of the twenty people.

challenge.question: What stands out about the speaker’s manner of speaking?
answers: He commands forcefully
He announces that everything is decided
He speaks humbly and cautiously
challenge.explanation: His respectful wording shows humility and care.

questions.question: What can we infer from the word “Peradventure”?
answers: The speaker is not certain that twenty will be found
The speaker is certain that twenty will be found
The speaker knows that no one will be found
questions.explanation: “Peradventure” expresses possibility or uncertainty.

questions.question: What does “for twenty’s sake” mean in this context?
answers: After twenty years have passed
For the sake of or because of twenty people
Because the city is twenty miles away
questions.explanation: The city would be spared because of the twenty people.

questions.question: What stands out about the speaker’s manner of speaking?
answers: He commands forcefully
He announces that everything is decided
He speaks humbly and cautiously
questions.explanation: His respectful wording shows humility and care.

paragraphs.title: Abraham’s Request for the Sake of Ten

easy.question: How many people does Abraham hope will be found in the city?
answers: Ten
Five
Forty
easy.explanation: Abraham says, “Peradventure ten shall be found there.”

easy.question: What does the Lord promise to do if ten people are found?
answers: Punish them
Not destroy the city
Bring them out of the city
easy.explanation: The Lord says, “I will not destroy it for ten’s sake.”

easy.question: What does Abraham ask at the beginning of his words?
answers: That the Lord give him money
That the Lord send angels
That the Lord not be angry and allow him to speak
easy.explanation: Abraham says, “Oh let not the Lord be angry, and I will speak.”

medium.question: What is the order of events in the verse?
answers: Abraham asks, and the Lord answers that He will not destroy the city
The Lord asks, and Abraham refuses
Abraham destroys the city, and then the Lord speaks
medium.explanation: Abraham makes the request, and the Lord answers that He will spare the city for ten.

medium.question: What does “for ten’s sake” mean?
answers: Before ten people
Because of the ten people
After ten people
medium.explanation: The context means that the Lord would spare the city because of the ten.

medium.question: Why is the Lord’s answer directly connected to Abraham’s request?
answers: Abraham asks about ten, and the Lord agrees not to destroy the city if ten are found
Abraham asks to be king, and the Lord agrees
Abraham asks to leave the land, and the Lord refuses
medium.explanation: The Lord answers the exact possibility Abraham raises.

challenge.question: What can we understand from the words “yet but this once”?
answers: Abraham intends to speak only one more time
Abraham has already stopped speaking
Abraham wants to restart the conversation
challenge.explanation: The words indicate one final or additional request after the earlier appeals.

challenge.question: What does “Peradventure” express in Abraham’s words?
answers: Certainty that ten people exist
The possibility that ten people may be found
Knowledge that not even one person exists
challenge.explanation: The word expresses possibility or hope, not certainty.

challenge.question: What central idea appears in the Lord’s answer?
answers: The city will be spared if ten people are found
Only one person can save the city
The number of people has no connection to destruction
challenge.explanation: The Lord explicitly says He will not destroy the city for the sake of ten.

questions.question: What can we understand from the words “yet but this once”?
answers: Abraham intends to speak only one more time
Abraham has already stopped speaking
Abraham wants to restart the conversation
questions.explanation: The words indicate one final or additional request after the earlier appeals.

questions.question: What does “Peradventure” express in Abraham’s words?
answers: Certainty that ten people exist
The possibility that ten people may be found
Knowledge that not even one person exists
questions.explanation: The word expresses possibility or hope, not certainty.

questions.question: What central idea appears in the Lord’s answer?
answers: The city will be spared if ten people are found
Only one person can save the city
The number of people has no connection to destruction
questions.explanation: The Lord explicitly says He will not destroy the city for the sake of ten.

paragraphs.title: The Conversation Ends and Abraham Returns

easy.question: Who went away after finishing speaking with Abraham?
answers: The Lord
Abraham
Lot
easy.explanation: The verse says, “The Lord went his way” after speaking with Abraham.

easy.question: With whom did the Lord speak?
answers: Lot
Abraham
Isaac
easy.explanation: The verse says that the Lord had been speaking with Abraham.

easy.question: Where did Abraham return?
answers: To Sodom
To his father’s house
To his place
easy.explanation: The verse ends by saying, “Abraham returned unto his place.”

medium.question: What happened immediately after the Lord finished speaking with Abraham?
answers: Abraham began a journey
The Lord went away, and Abraham returned to his place
